Since the changing of the sky life had become unpleasant for Char'li, Son of Dae-el. Though the Elders had assigned no blame many among the tribe held the opinion that he was responsible; after all was it not he who uncovered the coin laid down by the chaotic luck god Tymoro? And then after the God had personally requested that Char'li become his vassal he had turned him down and rejected his gifts. It was no wonder the Gods were upset.

Char'li sat as he had often done since his encounter with the Gods, between the large mushrooms grown by his tribe playing backgammon. Tymoro, God of luck and chance had taught the game to him during their last encounter and he had become quite enamoured with it. As usual his opponent was Sha'ne.

The two young Med'ja sat in silence, the rattle of the dice and the clattering of chips marking the game's progression. Sha'ne was the first to speak "so what do you think's going to happen?" her voice was quiet and devoid of her usual energy "I don't know" Char'li replied, looking up from the game board "So much has happened these past few summers and our world has grown so much. There are times when I don't even recognise myself" The cave rumbled with the sound of thunder as the heavens crashed overhead.

"I accept That the Gods are angry" Char'li continued picking up a handful of soil, letting it slip through his paw "But I do not believe that we are the focus of that anger. The Gods are powerful and though our numbers are many, compared to a God we are but dust on the wind.

"And what of Sha'fu?" Sha'ne wondered, "what role did he play in all this?" "I've wondered that myself" Char'li replied, removing a chip from the board "While it's true Sha'fu was a drunkard he was by no means an invalid, still, the timing of his disappearance is uncanny" Had Sha'fu run afoul of the Gods? or had he merely wandered off in pursuit of some imagined foe, his mind beguiled by drink and the memory of battles past?

The two continued their game, their fears leavened through their sharing, until, the last of his pieces removed from the board, Char'li was triumphant. "Why don't we play again?" Sha'ne asked, rearranging the pieces on the board.

"Alright then best two out of three."

Chief Ma'ten and his brother, the Shaman Se'Kin the blind sat alone in the Cave of Elders "Brother, have I ever told you the tale of Ta'Flo the firewalker? "No, Se'Kin" the Chief replied, "I don't believe you have" "well brother, throw another log on the fire and I shall share my tale..."

This story takes place in the time of Sa'Kee, third Chieftain of the Med'ja-Hom. The Cult of Umbralocht was still in its infancy with many young Shamans vying for power, one such shaman was Ta'met. Ta'met had spent many years studying the properties of fire and its transformative effects making many remarkable discoveries; That it purified all but the most tainted of foods, destroyed all but the most potent of toxins and that many trees relied on the ravages of a forest fire to bring forth new life.

Despite these discoveries Ta'met had gained very little respect amongst his peers for fire could not be consumed and therefore could not truly be understood. In desperation Ta'met had tried to consume the flames of his hearth and his body had paid the price for his failure, his arms and face lined with twisted scars, proof again of the fires transformative power.

An outcast among his brothers, Ta'met tried to seek solace within his former home but the tribe of Med'ja-Hom had become distrustful of the shaman's zeal and power and so barred them from returning to the comfort of the Burrows (for this was long before the time of reconciliation) With his heart broken and his soul weary Ta'met cast himself upon the fires of his hearth in hope that the Gods would grant him a swift death.

But death was not what the Gods had planned for Ta'met. In his last act he had discovered secret magics laid down by Umbralocht during the Age of Creation and in doing so transformed himself from flesh and bone into light and fire rising not as Ta'met but as Ta'Flo, the fire walker: a living embodiment of the power of Flox himself.

The anger of Ta'Flo was unrelenting, many of his brothers were struck down by the power of his flames, the forest bathed in his fury. An army was rallied against him; an alliance between the surviving members of the Cult of Umbralocht and the Tribe of the Med'ja-Hom. The two marched as one through the ashes of the inferno that had once been the forests in which they lived and hunted until at last they came upon the Fire Walker.

Volley upon volley of arrows and spears rained down upon Ta'Flo yet all were turned to ash by the heat of his flame "Your weapons of wood and stone cannot harm me" The Fire Walker boasted "I am the living flame, all shall be consumed and transformed by my power" many good men and women lost their lives that day, consumed by Ta'Flo's flame, and it was feared that our tribe had met its end. Yet, in our moment of need the Gods intervened.

Flox, God of Fire and Light had been watching as Ta'Flo struck down our brethren and had become very displeased with the fledgling Fire Walker. What audacity this mortal had to take his power and claim it for himself without providing proper tribute. It was unthinkable, after all a God had his reputation to uphold. Justice was required, a debt to be repaid.

So it was that Flox descended upon the battlefield to claim Ta'Flo for himself "WHO DARES PARTAKE OF MY POWER" The God roared appearing from within a brilliant fireball "It is I!" Ta'Flo cried "Ta'Flo the Fire Walker, master of the living flame" "SILENCE!" the God's voice was booming, a gale force threatening to extinguish all that the Fire Walker had wrought. "You are but a spark, an insignificant speck burning for an instant as it rises above the pyre only to be extinguished by its own arrogance, It was by my power you were given life young spark and by my power you shall be consumed."

Ta'Flo let out a terrible cry, a primal scream of fear and anger as his soul began to burn, the God's judgment called down. The fires dimmed, the smoke dispersed and in moments not a single spark remained of the once great Shamans power.

Flox stood before the remainder of the Med'ja forces in a field of ash, the remainder of Ta'Flo's soul floating above the palm of his open hand "This one shall remain mine, he shall serve me in another life." With his vengeance served, his tribute claimed, Flox, God of Fire and Light departed from the mortal realm and returned whence he came.

Ma'Ten, brother of Se'Kin and 9th Chieftain of the Med'ja-Hom tribe sat alone in the Cave of Elders, his brother having long since departed for the bough of his tree and the comfort of his nest. The Chieftain often sat alone after his wife and his kin had long since turned to rest, the weight of his role and the problems that he faced somehow eased by the fire's warmth. As he placed another log upon the fire Ma'Ten caught a glimpse of a flicker from within, a flicker that he almost took for a face staring back at him, glaring in anger.
